0x61b10f0.name: rocksdb::TracerHelper::ParseVersionStr
quirks: The value is the decimal concatenation of EVERY digit in the string, dots skipped: b'1.2.3.4' -> 1234, not a tuple. The loop walks the whole string from data[0], not just the part after the last dot.
Accumulation is 32-bit and wraps: b'42949672.9.5' (digits 4294967295) -> -1 as a signed int.
A string of only dots (b'..') parses to 0 and returns OK; a single dot (b'.') is an error.
rules: find('.') == npos -> kCorruption with the 47-byte message
find('.') == rfind('.') (exactly one dot) -> kCorruption with the 46-byte message
otherwise walk every byte: '.' skipped, '0'..'9' accumulate value = value * 10 + digit (32-bit wrap), any other byte -> kCorruption with the 46-byte message
on success *version = value (signed 32-bit) and the returned Status is OK (code 0, no state)
0x61b10f0.vtable_slot: not applicable (static helper; no vtable slot)

0x61b1260.name: rocksdb::TracerHelper::EncodeTrace
quirks: The payload length is stored as the LOW 32 bits of the payload size (mov %eax); a payload of 2**32 bytes or more would truncate the field. Untestable by construction here; the tool models the truncation exactly.
rules: append the type byte at +0x08 as one byte
append the payload size (+0x20, the std::string size) as 4 bytes little-endian (low 32 bits)
append the payload bytes (+0x18 pointer, +0x20 length)
each append checks the std::string capacity guard (0x3fffffffffffffff - size <= chunk -> std::length_error); the tool models the guard and raises LengthError_
0x61b1260.vtable_slot: not applicable (static helper; no vtable slot)
